title: Algorithm
summary: An algorithm is a finite description of an effective step-by-step procedure for a class of inputs.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared effective procedures context is fixed.

content.plain: An algorithm is a finite description of an effective step-by-step procedure for a class of inputs.
content.exact: A precise algorithm fixes an input representation, transition rules, output condition, and halting behavior; formal models include Turing machines and recursive functions.
content.example: Euclid's algorithm repeatedly replaces (a,b) by (b,a mod b) until b=0.
content.caveat: An informal recipe is not automatically an algorithm until its steps and representations are unambiguous.
